title: Validation & base value
blurb: Tests setPathData() valid-prefix truncation, WebIDL TypeErrors, empty-array attribute removal, the CSS d / SMIL base-value boundary, and migrating off SVGPathSegList and path-data-polyfill.
question: Which invalid inputs silently truncate via SVG's valid-prefix rule versus throwing TypeError, and does getPathData() reflect CSS d or SMIL animations?
result: Bad commands, wrong arity, NaN, and invalid arc flags truncate at the first bad segment rather than throwing; missing dictionary members throw TypeError; CSS d and SMIL animations are invisible to getPathData().
testedIn: Chrome 153 behind --enable-blink-features=SVGPathDataAPI; not verified in Chrome 160

friction.summary: setPathData() silently truncates at the first invalid segment and removes the d attribute on empty arrays in Chromium
friction.repro: Run the empty-array and invalid-segment cases in section 1: Chromium removes the d attribute on setPathData([]) whereas Firefox and the explainer leave d="", and malformed segments stop silently instead of throwing.
friction.workaround: Validate segment types, finite values, and arc flags before calling setPathData(), and check getAttribute('d') if distinguishing an empty path from a missing attribute.
